title: Eleven Lines
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：role　|　正文 319 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 role 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In the school play of that winter I was given a small ① role: the nurse, who appears twice and has eleven lines. Every part in a play is a role, however small it looks. My sister, who had acted every leading ② role since she was twelve, told me the truth at once: 'You will be invisible, and that is useful.'

I did not believe her. My sister has always been my ③ role model, so I copied her methods: highlights in the script, notes in the margin, a pencil behind each ear. ④ In my role as prompter — because a small part usually means extra work — I sat in the wings for eleven rehearsals and learned every line in the play, including my sister's. Such roles teach patience faster than leading ones.

Rehearsals taught me something else, too. Silence, I discovered, ⑤ plays a larger role than any sentence; the eleven lines I had envied were nothing beside one held pause. The stage manager, meanwhile, carried out every one of her duties with total patience, a ⑥ role for which nobody ever thanks you.

Three days before the performance our director fell ill. Nobody else knew the blocking, so I ⑦ took on the role she would have filled, running the rehearsal from the third row with the script on my knees. It lasted four hours, and two people cried, and I understood for the first time what a director actually does.

⑧ In the role of the nurse I was on stage for four minutes in total. Yet people still tell me which moment they remember: not the confession scene, not the fight, but the pause before my second line. Writers always talk about the ⑨ role of small things in a story, and I had never understood what they meant until that night. My sister sent me one message afterwards: 'You were invisible, and it ⑩ played the biggest role of the night.'

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. （戏剧、电影中的）角色
B. n. 职责；任务（承担的一项工作）
C. n. 身份；以……的身份（in one's role as）
D. 固定搭配：play a (large/small) role 起（大／小）作用
E. 固定搭配：take on a role 承担、接手某项工作／角色
F. 固定搭配：the role of ……的作用／职责
G. 固定搭配：role model 榜样
H. 固定搭配：leading/minor role 主角／配角

items.q: given a small role: the nurse
every leading role since she was twelve
has always been my role model
plays a larger role than any sentence
a role for which nobody ever thanks you
I took on the role she would have filled
In the role of the nurse
the role of small things in a story
it played the biggest role of the night

answers.why: 作者分到的是剧里的“护士”一角，有十一句台词，是戏剧角色。
leading role 与 small/minor role 相对，意为“主角”，说明姐姐多年来一直是主演。
role model 是固定搭配，意为“榜样”，作者模仿姐姐的排练方法。
in one's role as＋身份，意为“作为……”，这里指以提词员的身份在侧幕。
play a (large/small) role 意为“起作用”，此处说沉默比台词更起作用。
a role for which nobody thanks you 指“职责、差事”，舞台监督的活儿无人感谢。
take on the role 意为“承担、接手”，导演病倒后作者顶上她的工作。
同样是 in one's role as，意为“以……的身份”，此处指作为护士这个角色登台。
the role of＋抽象事物，意为“……的作用”，作家常谈小事在故事里的作用。
play the biggest role 与第 5 题同义，指那晚作用最大的恰恰是不起眼的表演。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 在那出戏里我得到一个只有十一句台词的角色。（role n.）
我姐姐一直是我心中的榜样。（role model）
作为提词员，我在侧幕坐了十一次排练。（in one's role as）
沉默有时比任何台词都更起作用。（play a role）
导演病倒后，我接手了她的工作。（take on the role）
最不起眼的细节往往在故事中起最大的作用。（the role of）
answers: I was given a role with only eleven lines in that play.
My elder sister has always been my role model.
In my role as prompter, I sat in the wings for eleven rehearsals.
Silence sometimes plays a larger role than any line.
When the director fell ill, I took on the role she had filled.
The smallest details often play the biggest role in a story.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 role 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In that play I was given the small role of the nurse, with only eleven lines.
My sister, my role model since childhood, had played every leading role since she was twelve.
In my role as prompter I sat in the wings for eleven rehearsals and learned the whole script.
I discovered that a pause sometimes plays a larger role than any sentence.
When our director fell ill three days before the performance, I took on the role she would have filled.
That night taught me the role of small things in a story, and how much patience any part demands.
